clue.text: Not 26's normal rate

definitions.meaning: ordinary everyday food, the opposite of the gourmet cooking at 26
the usual charge for a journey, as on a bus or train ticket

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both plain ordinary meals and the regular ticket price for travel.

clue.text: Poet and writer aboard the Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: being aboard a ship means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, as in the liner's name, followed by ER, Elizabeth Regina
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A poet and an author travel together on the famous ocean liner.
explanation.walkthrough: The liner's name splits into SS (steamship) and ER (Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher); PEN goes inside after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Bird 20 to cause a stir?

annotationWithheld.why: Bird 20 to cause a stir? (7): 20 down OVERATE read as OVER + ATE, so the one clue word '20' is both the reversal indicator (OVER, turning MINA to ANIM) and the letters ATE; the check refuses a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Died unknown, having eaten 10's weed

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

indicators.note: something that has eaten another thing holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, means of unknown name
10 down is DELICATESSEN, whose usual short form is deli

explanation.surface: Someone nameless died after a meal from the delicatessen's weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having eaten' puts the shop's short form inside the word for nameless; ANON is a standard crossword abbreviation for anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered plant usually treated as a garden weed.

clue.text: Sailor catches another up in the capital

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole thing is read from bottom to top
to catch something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
another sailor: AB, able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: One sailor grabs a shipmate in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' makes TABAR, and 'up', in a down entry, turns that round to read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Artistic movement's waveband receives gold 6s

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so these pieces sit inside

parts.note: FM, frequency modulation, is a radio waveband
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
VI is six in Roman numerals, so sixes are VIs

explanation.surface: A radio station takes in golden sixes for an art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition carries the 's of the clue: the answer is the movement's name, with 's read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauvism was the early twentieth-century painting movement of Matisse and Derain, known for wild colour.

clue.text: Composer-violinist's treatment captivates southern Italy

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to hold captive, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: rosin is the resin violinists rub on their bows
S is the abbreviation for south or southern
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A composer and violinist whose playing charms southern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer-violinist's' reads as one person, but the hyphen divides the definition from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian opera composer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Worker in the Treasury, formerly, has joints of 1 across

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fisc is an archaic word for a state treasury
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
the hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: A civil servant in the old Treasury has some cuts of meat for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is STANDARD FARE; this classic British takeaway is the archetype of plain everyday food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and chips is the classic everyday British meal, the very type of ordinary fare.

clue.text: African city, converting oxygen to energy, turned Portuguese, say

indicators.note: turned means the result is reversed
converting one thing to another swaps a letter for a new one

parts.note: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone from an African city who changed their ways became Portuguese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converting oxygen to energy' swaps O (oxygen's symbol) for E (energy), making NAIREBI; 'turned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese live on the Iberian peninsula, so they are an example of Iberians.

clue.text: Showing effects of a bumpy bus ride?

indicators.note: a bumpy ride throws things about, so these letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: A passenger is black and blue after a rough bus journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Showing effects of', with 'a' as a link; the whole clue also works as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bruised shows the marks left by knocks, the visible effects of a rough ride.

clue.text: Not 1 across (as in selected outlets)

indicators.note: letters that are let out are released and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A fancy shop is no place for plain fare, as in some chosen stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is STANDARD FARE; a delicatessen sells the opposite, fine and exotic foods. The bracketed aside hides the whole anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen sells fine prepared foods, as opposed to plain everyday fare.

clue.text: Garden implement takes type of beetle prisoner

indicators.note: the hoe takes the beetle in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hoe is a long-handled garden tool for weeding
the stag beetle has large antler-like jaws

explanation.surface: A gardener's hoe captures a beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held prisoner as security for a demand.

clue.text: 4 within hearing? It's not important

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in a court of law
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something whispered to four people is of no consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 down; here it is just the number in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial things are trifling and of little significance.

clue.text: Bottle opener very cunningly concealed

indicators.note: the letters lie concealed inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A bottle opener has been very craftily hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle opener' reads as a corkscrew, but 'Bottle' alone is the definition, in its slang sense of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, and so is nerve.

clue.text: Monica's in trouble and she won't get off lightly

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: the name and the S of 's both count as letters here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Monica has problems and is in for a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off' means fall asleep, not escape punishment; 'in trouble' looks like the indicator, but 'in' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleepless cannot easily drop off, so they won't get off lightly, punning on nodding off.

clue.text: Atheist, given parental guidance, provided 1 across in Rome

indicators.note: provided in the sense of prepared, so the letters are made up anew

parts.note: PG is the film rating for parental guidance

explanation.surface: An unbeliever with a parent's advice was given an ordinary Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is STANDARD FARE; pasta is the everyday food in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is the staple everyday pasta dish of Italy.

clue.text: Paralysis when model replaces learner in 8 province

indicators.note: one letter replaces another in the word

parts.note: 8 across is IBERIAN; Catalonia is a province of Spain
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A Spanish region is struck down when a model takes over from a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia is a state of stupor in which a person is immobile, a kind of paralysis.

clue.text: Yearning to penetrate paintings put up by the airway

indicators.note: to penetrate is to go into, so one piece goes inside
in a down entry, put up means reversed

parts.note: paintings are art
to ache for something is to yearn for it

explanation.surface: A longing to hang pictures by the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' reverses only the paintings, giving TRA; 'to penetrate' then places the yearning inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the main airway to the lungs.

clue.text: Weapon used to get free basic accommodation outside

indicators.note: the accommodation goes outside the other piece

parts.note: a tent is simple shelter
to rid is to free from

explanation.surface: A weapon used to win free camping.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, the weapon of Neptune.

clue.text: Revolutionary holding up half a fish

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, a revolutionary socialist

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word up gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A rebel holds up half a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' looks like a robbery; split it, as 'holding' and 'up half'.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Line ends with note about lots of fur

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ti, also te, is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: lots of a word is most of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: A railway route's final stops mention a lot of fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of' trims the fur's last letter; TI is the sol-fa note also spelt te.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations of railway lines, where the lines stop.

clue.text: Had more than enough of being forthright about a drug

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone overdid things by speaking frankly about narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to eat more than you need, past tense matching 'had'.

clue.text: First pilgrims to Bethlehem included sort of poet

indicators.note: one piece is included within the other

parts.note: first is written 1st, read as IST
the Magi were the wise men who travelled to Bethlehem

explanation.surface: The earliest travellers to Bethlehem included a kind of poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is written 1ST, with the 1 taken as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An Imagist belonged to the early twentieth-century school of poets such as Pound, writing in clear images.

clue.text: Subject to snap?

parts.note: a snap is a photo, a pic

explanation.surface: Something that might be photographed?
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion or writing.

clue.text: Make use of the quality of diamonds — without diamonds

indicators.note: without means leaving out

parts.note: diamonds are the hardest natural substance
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Exploit the hardness of gems, without gems.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the D out of HARDNESS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To harness something is to put it to use, like harnessing energy.

clue.text: Bent PC helps to discover haul

indicators.note: bent means twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman helps find something to drag away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like slang for a corrupt policeman, PC being a police constable; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To schlep is to haul or lug something heavy, from Yiddish.

clue.text: People with something in common take notice of dyke

indicators.note: the tribe takes the notice in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a tribe is a group sharing ancestry or customs
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Group members pay attention to an embankment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dyke' looks like an embankment; it is the slang word for a lesbian.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribade is an old word for a lesbian, for which dyke is a slang term.

clue.text: Euch! Is Auntie cooking fancy food?

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A child, disgusted, asks whether Auntie is making something posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Haute cuisine is elaborate high-class cooking, a refined kind of food.
